Activity: Window Watching. Sit by a window with {name} and point to things outside like trees or cars as they watch curiously.
Action: 1. Sit comfortably with {name} near a window.
2. Point to moving leaves or light.
3. Say “Look at that!” softly.
4. Pause and watch their eyes.
5. Smile when they focus.
6. Name what they see.
7. Stop when they lose interest.

Framing: normal eye-level mid-shot — full scene visible, soft background bokeh.
Tone: middle-class family home — real, lived-in, slightly less curated than a catalog shoot. Everyday family realism.
Pose: natural and candid, not stiff or staged — but the baby's attention and gaze are clearly directed at the focus of the activity (the object, toy, or person named in the action), so a parent instantly reads what is happening. Avoid a vacant or wandering off-camera stare. Anatomically realistic — every limb has a visible support surface, and every visible hand belongs to a fully-present person in frame.
Anatomy: detailed hands and feet — every finger and toe individually rendered, clearly separated digits, no fused or webbed digits, anatomically correct. Baby has a soft baby-fat torso and limbs — no visible muscle definition, no defined abs, no adult musculature. Smooth chubby baby softness. Include exactly the people the scene calls for — no extra, duplicated, or partial people, and no disembodied or floating hands; every hand connects to a person who is fully visible in the frame.
Clothing: the baby wears soft, light pastel everyday baby clothing (a onesie or romper). Never fully naked or topless. For a bath activity, show a clean diaper or modest cover only — never full nudity.
